title: Primitive recursiveness of the two-tape table skipper
statement: For every natural number $n$, the reader that processes a table of $n+1$ rows, applying the two-work-tape action-field skipper $27$ times per row and returning the unconsumed suffix, is primitive recursive jointly in $n$ and the Boolean-string input. Each action-field read requires a valid two-bit input-head movement, two valid work-tape fields, a valid two-bit output field, and a successor-state field that is either a single $0$ or a $1$ followed by a unary index smaller than $n+1$; the work-tape fields consist of an arbitrary two-bit write field and a movement field that rejects $01$.
